title: decommission-legacy-node-ci-scripts-migrate-to-hermetic-executor
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Replaces legacy node-based CI scripts with a hermetic Go executor; adds lockfile verification and workspace-level task caching to reduce job duplication and flakiness. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation:
We have accumulated many ad-hoc NodeJS scripts under /ci/scripts over the years. They are a source of intermittent failures (node/npm version drift), slow boot times in ephemeral CI runners, and duplicated logic across repo-level pipelines. This PR migrates the orchestration logic into a small hermetic Go executor (cmd/ci-runner) and replaces the most common entrypoints with thin wrappers. Goals: reduce CI flare-ups, speed up small jobs by avoiding heavyweight node boot, and centralize lockfile enforcement in CI so dependency drift is caught early.

What this PR does (single-string description):
- Adds cmd/ci-runner: a single-binary task runner that reads a ci.yaml from the workspace and executes named tasks with hermetic environment setup (GOMODCACHE isolation, pinned npm/yarn wrappers for legacy tasks). The runner is intentionally minimal and uses the existing toolchain images in CI.
- Migrates lint/test/publish entrypoints to use ci-runner and consolidates duplicated matrix definitions in .github/workflows/ci.yaml.
- Introduces lockfile verification step: scripts/verify-lockfiles.sh (invoked by runner) which fails builds when package-lock.json or pnpm-lock.yaml drift is detected.
- Adds repo-level workspace cache keys for node_modules and go/pkg/mod and uses prefix-based partial restores to reduce wall time on repeated jobs.
- Removes ~600 lines of legacy bash/node glue under ci/scripts and replaces with small shim wrappers where necessary for backwards compatibility.
- Adds unit tests for ci-runner (internal) and a lightweight integration smoke test in .github/workflows/ci.yaml that runs only on a canary branch.

Checklist (what I validated):
- [x] Local unit tests for ci-runner (go test ./cmd/ci-runner)
- [x] CI matrix dry-run with a canary branch (ran three times to validate cache key behavior)
- [x] Verified lockfile verification fails when package-lock.json is modified without updating lockfile
- [x] Ensured existing release automation still triggers when head contains release/* tags

Commits (high-level):
- feat(ci): add hermetic Go executor and core task runner
- refactor(ci): migrate lint/test tasks to runner and remove node script duplications
- feat(ci): add lockfile verification and cache-key strategy
- test(ci): add integration smoke job and unit tests for runner
- chore(ci): remove legacy scripts and update docs

Files changed (representative):
["cmd/ci-runner/main.go", "internal/runner/* (new)", ".github/workflows/ci.yaml", "ci/verify-lockfiles.sh", "ci/scripts/lint.sh -> wrappers/lint.sh (thin)", "tools/cache-keys.md", "Makefile (ci targets)"]

Testing notes and perf impact:
- Average cold-start time for small lint jobs went from ~30s to ~9s in our canary runs due to avoiding Node install boot where possible and reusing cached toolchains.
- Cache hit rate stabilized at ~82% on repeat runs after the new keying strategy.
- One flaky lint job was traced to a preexisting rule in eslint that relied on transient environment variables; addressed as part of the migration.

Rollback plan:
- The migration keeps thin wrappers for all public entrypoints. If a regression is found, revert the single merge commit and CI will resume using the previous node scripts. The earlier commit has a tag with the old scripts preserved for emergency rollbacks.

How to review (practical pointers):
- Start with cmd/ci-runner/main.go to validate security/sandboxing assumptions. The runner does not execute arbitrary shell code by default; tasks are defined in ci.yaml and are run with explicit env and process isolation.
- Check .github/workflows/ci.yaml for matrix consolidation and new cache steps.
- Verify ci/verify-lockfiles.sh for the exact failure mode we will see on drift.

Related work and context: ENG-2021 is the follow-up to extract more workflows into the runner. ENG-2045 is the tracking ticket for expanding runner features to private deploys. SUP-781 surfaced the initial incident (CI flakes due to node/npm mismatch) that prompted this change.

Merge and rollout summary:
- Merged via squash by Lara Singh on 2026-02-26 after final approval and successful CI on the canary branch.
- Post-merge actions: small monitoring check in dashboards for next 48h focusing on cache hit rate and lint job latency.
commits_summary: 5 commits: add hermetic Go executor; migrate main tasks; add lockfile checks; add integration smoke tests; remove legacy scripts
review_comments:
Evan: Please confirm the runner's environment isolation prevents access to host's GITHUB_TOKEN by default.
Maya: The runner only exposes tokens explicitly passed via ci.yaml; GITHUB_TOKEN is not auto-injected.

Lara: Can we keep a short lived toggle to run old node scripts in case of emergency?
Maya: Added a feature flag RUN_LEGACY_SCRIPTS and a recovery section in docs.

Samir: Nit: prefer smaller cache key window to avoid stale modules.
Maya: Reduced key scope to include commit timestamp bucket (15m) per our discussion which preserves cache locality while bounding staleness.

Evan: Observability - add tracing span for task execution.
Maya: Added basic OpenTelemetry span around task execution, hooks in runner for future extensions.
